prompt:
You are writing the voice-over for a 3-minute hackathon demo video of AccessPoint, an assistant for people who struggle with self-service machines (older people, blind and low-vision people, migrants). The video is judged by busy hackathon judges.

Rules for every line:
- Plain, warm, confident English. Short sentences. No jargon, no hype words ("revolutionary", "seamless", "cutting-edge"), no em dashes.
- At most 12 words per line, so each fits one caption.
- About 2.6 words per second of speaking time: never write more lines than fit the scene's seconds.
- Only state facts given in the scene description. Never invent numbers or features.
- Name Meta's models exactly: Muse Spark, SAM 3.1, Muse Voice.

Scenes (id, seconds, what's on screen):
- hero (5 s): A woman's voice says 'I can't read this screen. Help me.' Narrator follows with one line about how common this is.
- brand (3 s): Logo and tagline 'Stuck at a machine? Send a photo. Get the next step.'
- problem (8 s): Machines replaced counters just as the world ages (1.4B people 60+ by 2030, 2.2B with vision impairment, 281M migrants). Then: a general chatbot at a machine can do harm (wrong button, guesses, rushes).
- arch (12 s): How it works, four nodes lit in turn: Muse Spark reads the photo and plans one step; SAM 3.1 outlines every button precisely; code points only where the two agree and stops anything you didn't ask for; Muse Voice hears answers in 25 languages.
- guard (7 s): Guardrails: never needs your PIN, asks instead of guessing, stops wrong totals and transfers, you press every button yourself.
- demo-airport (24 s): App demo 1: Amara, first flight, scans the 'Need help? Scan me' sticker on the check-in kiosk, one Start button, puts passport on the reader, answers 'yes' and 'window' by voice, boarding pass prints. Narrator has 2 short lines; the app speaks the rest.
- demo-checkout (14 s): App demo 2: Siti, a helper in Singapore, at an English self-checkout, hears every step in Bahasa Indonesia, including 'unexpected item in the bagging area'. 1 narrator line.
- demo-ticket (12 s): App demo 3: Daniel is blind; AccessPoint guides his hand to the card slot of a train ticket machine. 1 narrator line.
- demo-mismatch (12 s): Safety 1: Mr Lim buys one carton of milk, the self-checkout total says S$42.00 instead of S$4.20; AccessPoint says stop, press Cancel. 1 narrator line.
- demo-glare (8 s): Safety 2: glare hides the screen; it asks for a better angle instead of guessing. 1 narrator line.
- chat-telegram (15 s): No app needed: the same assistant in a chat. Telegram, live: Amara sends a photo of the seat screen; real Muse Spark answer asks window or aisle; she taps Window 14A; it says where it is and sends a voice note. 2 narrator lines.
- chat-whatsapp (14 s): WhatsApp: Siti sends a photo, gets the step in Bahasa Indonesia, as text and a voice note. 1-2 narrator lines.
- chat-messenger (14 s): Messenger: Mr Lim sends a photo of the S$42 total; it says stop. Scan the sticker, chat opens, nothing to install. 1-2 narrator lines.
- results (6 s): We measured it on the real models: Muse Spark 7 of 7 screens right, Spark plus SAM 3.1 pointed at the right button 5 of 5, Muse Voice understood 3 of 3 languages, 20 of 20 bot tests, 11 of 11 app flows.
- close (6 s): Close: 'Independence by design.' Try it in your browser, link and QR on screen. Built on Meta's models.
